metaDescription: Five detail sanders under $30 compared on pad shape, orbits per minute, amp draw, dust handling and whether a mouse, file or pen sander fits your corners.
expertTake: A detail sander under $30 is a small corded tool for corners, spindles and trim, and the HYCHIKA is the best overall because it runs at 1.6 amps and up to 14,000 orbits per minute with a six-hole dust system and 12 sheets in the box. The WEN 6301 is the pick for a larger, angled pad, the DEKOPRO is the cheap bundle with 15 sheets, and the WEN 6307 file sander and SHALL pen sander handle slots and tight profiles the others cannot reach. Skip this tier for flat panels, because a detail sander is slow on open surfaces.
introParagraphs: A detail sander has a small pad, often a triangle, that fits into corners and tight shapes a larger sander cannot reach. It is a niche tool but a handy one, and it costs little enough that most workshops keep one for chair spindles, louvered doors and window sashes.

Under thirty dollars the design matters more than the specifications, since each shape of sander does a different job. This guide explains which style fits which task, what the speed numbers mean, and how to avoid the dust and clogging problems that plague cheap models. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below match each sander to a job.

products.name: HYCHIKA 14,000 OPM Detail Sander, 1.6 Amp, 6-Hole Dust Collection

specList.label: Suited to
specList.value: Wood, metal and plastic in tight spaces

products.description:
The HYCHIKA is the best buy because it pairs the strongest motor in the group, 1.6 amps, with the highest orbit rate at up to 14,000 OPM. Orbits per minute is the number that counts for a detail sander, because the small pad has to cut quickly to be useful in a corner. A faster orbit takes more material off per pass without pressing harder.

A six-hole dust collection system routes dust through holes in the pad into a bag, which keeps sandpaper from clogging and keeps the cut line visible. In a corner the sandpaper clogs fast, and clogged paper burns the wood, so dust pickup matters more here than on a large sander. The kit includes 12 sheets in P80, P120 and P240, so you can run a coarse-to-fine sequence immediately.

Against the DEKOPRO, which is a 1 amp tool, the HYCHIKA has a more powerful motor and a dust bag, and against the WEN 6301 it offers a faster orbit. Replace the paper before it glazes, and work with the tip of the triangle in corners, since pressing the whole pad flat on a small area removes too much material. Rotate the paper as the tip dulls so the pad keeps cutting, and replace it when all three corners are worn.
products.bestFor: Anyone who sands trim, furniture corners and louvers and wants the strongest motor here.
pros: 1.6 amp motor is the strongest in the group
Up to 14,000 OPM cuts quickly in corners
Six-hole dust system keeps paper clean
cons: Triangular pad wears at the tip
Less established brand for replacement pads

products.name: WEN 6301 Electric Detailing Palm Sander, 1 Amp, 13,500 OPM
products.description:
The WEN 6301 is the largest-pad sander here, with a 3.75 by 5.5 inch pad and an angled tip for precision work. A bigger pad covers more area per pass, which makes it faster than the mouse-style sanders on flat sections between corners, while the angled tip reaches into the corners themselves. That combination makes it a good compromise between a detail sander and a quarter-sheet sander.

Its one-amp motor delivers 13,500 OPM, a quick orbit for a light tool, and it weighs only two pounds, so it will not tire your hand during a long session of window sashes or cabinet doors. Against the HYCHIKA, it has a lower amp rating but a bigger pad, which spreads the effort.

The WEN is the lowest-priced option in the lineup, which makes it a sensible first detail sander. Use hook-and-loop or adhesive sheets cut to size, and replace them often, since small sheets wear out quickly. Do not press hard, because a one-amp motor slows noticeably under load and leaves swirls. Work from the tip of the pad into the corner, never from the flat toward the tip, which can chew the edge.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a larger pad with an angled tip at the lowest price.
pros: Largest pad in the group at 3.75 x 5.5 inches
13,500 OPM orbit rate for a light tool
Only two pounds, so easy on the hand
cons: No dust bag or extras listed
Pad is bigger than a true mouse sander

products.name: DEKOPRO 1A Electric Mouse Detail Sander, 13,000 RPM, 15 Sheets
products.description:
The DEKOPRO is the sander that arrives with the most paper. Fifteen four-hole sheets in P60, P120, P240, P400 and P1,000 give you three of each grit, which covers rough shaping, smoothing and a fine finish. A full grit progression is the secret to a smooth detail job, and having all five grits in the box saves buying a set.

Its 100W motor is about one amp, and the 13,000 RPM figure is a no-load speed, a different measure from orbits per minute, so it is not directly comparable with the HYCHIKA's 14,000 OPM. The kit includes both a dust bag and an extraction hose, which gives you the option of connecting a vacuum, a feature that many cheap sanders skip.

It is a mouse-style sander with a small triangular pad, ideal for tight spaces. Against the WEN 6301, it has a smaller pad but more sandpaper and a dust hose. Keep a stock of sheets since small pads consume paper quickly, and match the four-hole pattern to the sheets you buy. Test the sander on scrap before working a finished surface, and keep a light touch.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want a full grit set and a vacuum hose in one box.
pros: Dust bag and vacuum hose both included
Compact mouse shape reaches tight spaces
cons: RPM figure is not directly comparable with OPM

products.name: WEN 6307 Variable Speed Detailing File Sander, 1/2 x 18 Inch Belt
products.description:
The WEN 6307 is a different kind of sander: a belt file. A narrow 1/2 by 18 inch belt runs over a nose that pivots up to 55 degrees, so it reaches into slots, curved edges and the inside of cutouts where a triangular pad cannot go. It is the tool for smoothing scroll-saw cuts, the inside of a chair arm or a curved bracket.

Variable speed from 1,080 to 1,800 feet per minute lets you slow down for delicate shaping or speed up for stock removal, and the auto-tracking belt means you never tension or adjust it. Belt sanding removes material faster than an orbital action, so it takes a lighter touch. Against the HYCHIKA, it handles profiles instead of corners.

Because a belt cuts aggressively, keep it moving and work with the grain when possible. The 1/2 inch width suits slots and curves, not flat surfaces. Replace belts when they glaze, and keep a few grits on hand, since belt sizes are specific to the tool. Replace belts as soon as they glaze, because a glazed belt burns the wood and slows the cut.
products.bestFor: Woodworkers who sand curves, slots and cutouts that pads cannot reach.
pros: Narrow belt reaches slots and tight curves
cons: Belts are tool-specific and must be bought separately
Aggressive cut can gouge if pressed

products.name: SHALL Mini Pen Sander, 4 Speeds, 8 Sanding Heads, Corded

specList.label: Heads
specList.value: 8 shapes including square, slim and triangular

products.description:
The SHALL pen sander is the most precise tool in the group. Its slender body is held like a pen, and a reciprocating head moves the sanding tip back and forth in a tiny stroke. It comes with eight heads, including square, rectangular, slim and triangular shapes, so you can match the tip to a groove, a corner or a carved detail.

Four speeds let you control the aggressiveness, and the pen shape lets you sand with fingertip control, which is why it is popular with model makers and furniture restorers. It is not a stock removal tool, because the head moves in a short stroke with little power. Against the HYCHIKA, it can reach grooves and carved details that no pad can, but it removes material far more slowly.

Use it for finishing touches on small, intricate parts, and keep the sandpaper fresh since small heads wear fast. A corded pen sander is lighter than a pad sander and gives a steady feed, but its small size means it overheats if you press hard. Let it run at a comfortable pace. Take frequent breaks, since a small corded tool heats up in a long session.
products.bestFor: Model makers, restorers and anyone sanding carved or very small details.
cons: Small heads wear and need replacing

buyingCriteria.explanation: A triangular mouse pad, as on the DEKOPRO and HYCHIKA, reaches corners. The WEN 6301's larger pad with an angled tip covers more area. The WEN 6307's belt reaches slots and curves, and the SHALL pen sander reaches carvings. Choose the shape that matches your hardest spot first. A good rule is to choose the sander for the hardest spot on the project, because the easy spots can be handled with any tool.

The HYCHIKA lists 14,000 OPM and the WEN 6301 13,500 OPM, while the DEKOPRO lists 13,000 RPM and the WEN 6307 lists belt speed in feet per minute. These are different measures and are not directly comparable. Compare like with like, and prefer OPM for pad sanders. A pad sander's triangle tip does the real work in a corner, so keep the tip fresh by rotating the sheet when one corner wears.

Small pads clog fast, and clogged paper burns the wood. The HYCHIKA's six-hole system and the DEKOPRO's hose help. Connect a vacuum whenever you sand, since a small bag fills in minutes. A vacuum hose also reduces hand fatigue, because the hose supports part of the weight and keeps dust off your arm.

Detail sanders use small, shape-specific sheets that wear out quickly. The DEKOPRO includes 15 sheets and the HYCHIKA 12. Check that replacement sheets are sold in standard sizes, since proprietary shapes cost more and sell out. Buy a variety pack of sheets before you start, since a run to the store mid-project interrupts the finish.

At 1 to 1.6 amps these sanders are light-duty tools. The HYCHIKA's 1.6 amps is the strongest, and the DEKOPRO and WEN 6301 are about one amp. Pressing harder does not speed the work and slows the orbit. A light touch with a one-amp motor is better than a heavy hand, because pressure only stalls the orbit.

A corner shows scratches more than a flat. Work from 80 to 120 to 240, as the HYCHIKA's sheets allow. Skipping grits leaves scratches that show under finish, and a detail sander removes material slowly enough that skipping rarely saves time. Wipe the surface with a tack cloth between grits to avoid dragging coarse grit across the finer pass.

specDecoder.meaning: OPM counts how often the pad completes an orbit. Higher means faster cutting. A mouse sander's name comes from its shape, which is rounded at the back and pointed at the front.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not compare RPM with OPM, as the DEKOPRO's 13,000 RPM is a different measure.

specDecoder.meaning: FPM measures belt speed on a belt sander, like the WEN 6307's 1,080 to 1,800. A belt sander removes material by cutting along the belt, which is why it is more aggressive than an orbital pad.
specDecoder.watchFor: A belt cuts faster than a pad at the same power.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps measure current draw, a proxy for motor size. Even a one-amp motor draws enough current to heat a thin cord, so do not use a coiled extension cord.
specDecoder.watchFor: At this size, amps are low across the board.

specDecoder.meaning: Hook and loop lets you change sheets quickly, while adhesive sheets are cheaper but stick once. Adhesive-backed sheets stay put better on a small pad but cost more over time.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check which type the sander uses before buying paper.

specDecoder.meaning: Holes in the pad that draw dust through to a bag or hose. A pad with no dust holes will clog quickly, so choose one with holes if you work with softwood.
specDecoder.watchFor: Match the hole pattern of sheets to the pad.

maintenance.why: Glazed paper burns wood. Unplug before changing paper.
A full bag cuts suction. Clean the pad face with a brush.
Dust packs the hook face. Check the dust bag seam.
A damaged cord is a hazard. Inspect the cord strain relief.
A worn pad loses sheets. Store it dry.

faq.q: What is a detail sander used for?
faq.a: Corners, spindles, trim and tight spots where a larger sander cannot fit. Wear a dust mask, and sand outside or with a vacuum when possible.

faq.q: Can I use it on flat surfaces?
faq.a: You can, but it is slow. Use a random orbital sander instead. Replace the sheet when the cut slows, since worn paper rubs rather than cuts.
Start with 80 or 120 and finish with 240. Use the sander at a slight angle so the leading edge does the work.
Yes. Small pads clog fast and dust is a health hazard.

faq.q: Are belt file sanders worth it?
faq.a: For slots and curves, yes. They cut quickly.
Keep the sander moving and use light pressure.
